reference.description: User-shared screenshot: BR-01, FR-001 through FR-008, TS-001 through TS-037. Scenario names and disputed claims transcribed for reference only.

businessRequirement.statement: Validate Mastercard credit purchase artefacts against the applicable ATL105 message, amount, response and lifecycle requirements; establish brand identity and external acceptance through separately evidenced policies and execution.
businessRequirement.scope: POS credit Purchase/Capture using transaction type 0 and credit card type 020; other entry modes, related lifecycle legs and post-authorization interfaces are conditional, not implicitly approved.

creditExpiry.anchor: The device performs expiration date validation in a credit card transaction.

partial.anchor: A Partial Approval transaction enables a merchant to receive approval for the amount available

receipt.anchor: This section discusses the following information that must print on credit card receipts:

receiptPan.anchor: The Account Number (Element No. 2) must be truncated

receiptExpiry.anchor: The Expiration Date must be suppressed on all transaction receipts.

network.anchor: No compatibility policy is bundled because ATL105 does not define a complete brand

lessons.statement: Account Number is Element 2, not Element 24; validate the declared non-TransArmor, track, token or encrypted representation rather than applying a universal numeric-only constraint.

The device validates credit-card expiry. For manual account entry, Element 12 carries expiry in MMYY format; Element 51 is not the expiry field. The requirement to send expiry even for expired-card authorizations is not a blanket local rejection rule.
In the scoped credit purchase context Element 78 is 0020: transaction type 0 plus financial card type 020. Neither 020 nor 0020 alone proves Mastercard brand identity.

Sequence Number is Element 86, not Element 80; it is six digits in 000001-999999 for the scoped financial flow. Related preauthorized completion, reversal and cancellation legs retain the applicable original sequence; unrelated new transactions receive a new sequence.
Approval Number is Element 5 with six alphanumeric characters; Element 6 is Approved Amount. Preserve the original approval reference when required by the specific follow-up flow.

Financial requests carry Element 55, Element 63 and Segment 100 in the source-defined layout; count transmitted segments and apply companion-segment conditions. Format compliance does not prove host acceptance.

Fuel Amount is Element 41, Nonfuel Amount is Element 58 and Segment 100 Tax Amount is Element 99, not PC Tax Element 74. In the scoped Mastercard case these fields have up to seven digits with two assumed decimal places; apply presence and discount rules separately.
Cash Amount Element 17 describes cash back and uses up to eight numeric digits with two assumed decimal places. Its existence does not establish Mastercard credit cash-back eligibility.

Interpret Element 83 in its transaction context: 0 is Purchase/Capture approval, 2 is authorization-only approval and 1 is communications-test approval but decline for other transactions. Format validity is not an issuer outcome.

Partial Approval Indicator is Element 121. For supported credit partial-approval contexts with indicator 1, response F and Element 6 identify partial approval and approved amount; prompt for the remaining balance. Indicator 5 is not a generic Mastercard partial-approval value.

Use the 30-second response interval and source-defined late-response handling. An eligible TOR retains the original sequence; do not infer TOR eligibility for all authorization or completion contexts.

For the Section 2.3.1 same-device queued-TOR flow, transmit the queued TOR before the next financial request from that device. Do not impose a global single-thread restriction on unrelated devices or flows.
Credit receipts use the source-defined content and Mastercard receipt identifier MC; mask the account to the last four digits and suppress expiry. Receipt production is not settlement evidence.

questions.question: Provide the approved Mastercard BIN/IIN service, versioned ranges, trusted processor brand evidence and routing/eligibility policy; specify treatment of disagreement, tokens and co-badged cards.
questions.evidenceNeeded: Versioned provider and routing policy, synthetic identity test vectors, target environment and owner.

questions.question: Which trusted service supplies active, blocked, lost/stolen status, and what are the permitted offline, unavailable-service and expiry rejection outcomes? Provide PAN length/checksum policy and expiry boundary/timezone rules.
questions.evidenceNeeded: Card-validation contract, synthetic issuer cases and explicit failure outcomes.

questions.question: Provide merchant ID/MCC mappings and merchant-active/purchase-eligibility configuration, including negative outcomes.
questions.evidenceNeeded: Versioned configuration and synthetic merchant profiles.

questions.question: Which Appendix J entry-mode encodings and conditional EMV/contactless/e-commerce companion data are in scope for this Mastercard purchase pack?
questions.evidenceNeeded: Source-backed entry-mode/context matrix and approved synthetic request fixtures.

questions.question: Specify the purchase-total field and reconciliation formula, currency source, zero/negative handling, discounts, and whether cash back is permitted for the scoped Mastercard credit product.
questions.evidenceNeeded: Exact field mapping and product policy with boundary cases; do not generalize debit cash-back rules.

questions.question: Provide synthetic request and response fixtures and expected full approval, decline and partial approval outcomes, including response/approval/amount correlation.
questions.evidenceNeeded: Versioned simulator or host oracle; expected and actual outcomes must remain separate.

questions.question: Confirm transport mode, same-device TOR queue handling, late responses, retry policy, route limits and the separate recommended TOR forwarding delay. Resolve any source timing/attempt-summary ambiguity.
questions.evidenceNeeded: Applicable Sections 2.3.1-2.3.4 interpretation and deterministic transport tests.

questions.question: Provide the clearing-record format, settlement protocol, reconciliation totals, response meanings and original authorization reference requirements.
questions.evidenceNeeded: Authoritative clearing/settlement contracts and synthetic end-to-end evidence; ATL105 request validity is insufficient.

questions.question: Define audit events, permitted masked fields, retention, access controls and reconciliation evidence. How are PAN and sensitive authentication data excluded or protected?
questions.evidenceNeeded: Approved audit/security policy and redacted log examples; no production card data.

scenarios.name: Card Number Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: PAN numeric; Mastercard BIN valid; length valid; Luhn passes; card active; proceeds to authorization.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Separate raw-PAN checks, trusted Mastercard identity and issuer status from ATL105 account-field representation.
validations: Check declared account-entry representation against Element 2.
Apply PAN/BIN/Luhn/status checks only using the approved external policy.
scenarios.expected: Report bounded field checks and external-policy gaps; no inferred authorization.

scenarios.name: Expiry Date Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Element 51 present for manual entry; MMYY, length 4, not past current date.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use Element 12 for manual expiry and perform credit expiry validation; distinguish malformed/expired checks from required transmission for expired-card authorizations.
validations: Manual expiry is MMYY in Element 12, not Element 51.
Apply Section 10.1.1.1 century handling through 1249.
Do not suppress required expiry merely because it is expired.
scenarios.expected: Correct field/format checks; local expired-card disposition awaits policy.

scenarios.name: Card Status Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Card active, not blocked/lost/stolen/expired; purchase continues.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Obtain account eligibility from a trusted status service or simulator; request data cannot establish active-card status.
validations: Bind service identity, response timestamp and declared outcome to the case.
Keep unavailable status explicit.
scenarios.expected: Eligibility result only with external evidence; otherwise review required.

scenarios.name: Processing Code Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Processing Code = Purchase/Capture (020).
scenarios.correctedRequirement: For this POS credit Purchase/Capture use Element 78 Prompt Code 0020, not standalone 020.
validations: Transaction type 0 and financial card type 020 form four-character 0020.
Do not infer Mastercard identity from credit code 020.
scenarios.expected: Classified as credit Purchase/Capture; brand/routing acceptance remains separate.

scenarios.name: Entry Mode Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Swipe, EMV, contactless, manual and e-commerce values allowed.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Validate exact Appendix J encodings and conditional companion data for the declared entry context; do not treat labels as wire values.
validations: Require explicit entry context and versioned encoding.
Apply EMV/contactless/e-commerce dependencies only when source-supported.
scenarios.expected: Mapped entry-mode checks or explicit unresolved-context finding.

scenarios.name: Merchant Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Merchant ID present; merchant active; MCC valid; transaction accepted.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Separate merchant field mapping from configured active status and Mastercard purchase eligibility.
validations: Bind identity/MCC to declared configuration.
Use approved synthetic active/inactive profiles.
scenarios.expected: No transaction-acceptance claim without configuration and execution evidence.

scenarios.name: Message Format Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Element 55 populated; version supported; mandatory fields populated; accepted by BuyPass.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Validate Element 55 and financial request layout, including conditional data; report format compliance separately from host acceptance.
validations: Use six-character message-format identifier and source-defined financial layout.
Apply conditional companion-segment rules.
scenarios.expected: Only applicable structural checks pass; host acceptance is not executed.

scenarios.name: Segment Count Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Element 63 populated; count matches transmitted segments.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Element 63 must match the actual source-defined transmitted segment count, not merely the number of JSON objects.
validations: Calculate from serialized segment composition.
Reject a count mismatch in a controlled mutation.
scenarios.expected: Count predicate outcome only, not successful host parsing.

scenarios.name: Standard Message Data Segment Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Segment 100 required/present; request accepted.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Require Segment 100 in the financial request layout; presence alone does not establish full request validity.
validations: Confirm correct segment identity and layout.
Check other applicable fields/segments separately.
scenarios.expected: Presence/layout assertion only.

scenarios.name: Account Number Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Element 24 present; numeric only; no delimiters/control characters.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use Element 2, not Data Type Indicator Element 24; validate the declared account-entry/TransArmor representation.
validations: Do not apply numeric-only constraints to an encoded track/token/encryption composite.
Check source-defined length and separator treatment for the chosen context.
scenarios.expected: Scoped account representation check, not card/account approval.

scenarios.name: Purchase Amount Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Amount > 0, numeric, currency supplied, valid decimal precision.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Bind purchase amount and currency to explicit fields and source-defined encoding and reconciliation rules before asserting pass/fail.
validations: Do not invent a generic amount/currency JSON mapping.
Keep total and component rules separate.
scenarios.expected: Review required until exact total/currency contract is supplied.

scenarios.name: Fuel Amount Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Fuel amount contains total fuel purchase value.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use Element 41 with applicable fuel/discount rules; Mastercard uses the non-Amex seven-digit maximum and two assumed decimal places.
validations: Include when fuel is sold.
Apply net fuel and mixed fuel/nonfuel discount rules.
scenarios.expected: Bounded fuel representation check; total reconciliation requires fixture policy.

scenarios.name: Non-Fuel Amount Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Amount numeric and >= 0.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Element 58 excludes fuel, tax and cash and uses up to seven digits for Mastercard with two assumed decimal places; do not automatically admit zero from a generic >=0 claim.
validations: Apply presence, valid-value and discount rules in the selected context.
Distinguish missing optional value from a zero-valued field.
scenarios.expected: Scoped nonfuel checks; zero/omission context remains explicit.

scenarios.name: Tax Amount Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Tax amount numeric and precision valid.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use Segment 100 Element 99, not PC Tax Element 74; apply its seven-digit Mastercard limit, assumed decimals and source-defined applicability.
validations: Validate digits/range and context.
Do not equate segment tax with purchase-card tax.
scenarios.expected: Tax predicate only; applicability/reconciliation still requires context.

scenarios.name: Cash Amount Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Numeric cash amount allowed when business rules met.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Element 17 describes cash back; do not infer eligibility for Mastercard credit from this field's existence.
validations: If separately authorized by product policy, validate up to eight digits and two assumed decimal places.
Keep unsupported/unknown cash-back context review-gated.
scenarios.expected: No Mastercard cash-back acceptance without product policy.

scenarios.name: Sequence Number Generation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Element 80 present, length 6, unique value.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use Element 86, not Purchase Code Element 80; check six digits and range 000001-999999 for this financial scope and uniqueness for unrelated transactions.
validations: Reject length/range mutations.
Check generation using device/history evidence, not one isolated payload.
scenarios.expected: Format result and separately evidenced generation/correlation result.

scenarios.name: Sequence Number Retention
scenarios.referenceClaim: Purchase, response, reversal, settlement retain same sequence.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Retain Element 86 for source-defined associated financial legs; settlement-interface correlation requires its own contract.
validations: Bind original and follow-up requests explicitly.
Do not reuse the same sequence for unrelated new transactions.
scenarios.expected: Applicable lifecycle predicate only; settlement correlation unresolved.

scenarios.name: Mastercard Credit Identification
scenarios.referenceClaim: Network Mastercard, card program Credit, transaction Purchase.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Combine trusted brand evidence with credit purchase context; 0020 does not independently establish Mastercard.
validations: Resolve explicit brand from trusted evidence.
Reject disagreement through the network-policy contract.
scenarios.expected: Review required without brand and eligibility policy.

scenarios.name: Routing Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Network selection matches Mastercard routing rules; transaction reaches issuer.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Validate against an approved routing policy and observe dispatch separately from issuer receipt.
validations: Bind selected route, identity evidence and policy version.
Use simulator or network trace evidence without card secrets.
scenarios.expected: No issuer-receipt claim from route selection alone.

scenarios.name: Authorization Request Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: All mandatory ATL105 elements present; request accepted by issuer.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Check all context-applicable request fields and serialization, then separately observe host/issuer outcome.
validations: Validate complete declared context, not only Segment 100 presence.
Keep external outcome Not Executed without a run.
scenarios.expected: Structural outcome only until host/simulator evidence exists.

scenarios.name: Response Reception Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Response format valid; response successfully interpreted.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Parse the applicable financial response, correlate it to the request and interpret Element 83 in context.
validations: Use actual or controlled synthetic response evidence.
Do not treat request validity as proof of response receipt.
scenarios.expected: Correlated parsed response only when response data exists.

scenarios.name: Approval Number Capture
scenarios.referenceClaim: Element 6 received for approval; approval stored.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Capture Approval Number Element 5; Element 6 is Approved Amount, not the approval identifier.
validations: Validate six-character alphanumeric approval field in its applicable response.
Keep approved amount as an independent value.
scenarios.expected: Correct field mapping; persistence needs observed execution.

scenarios.name: Approval Number Retention
scenarios.referenceClaim: Approval available for settlement and reversals.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Preserve Element 5 where the source requires the original approval reference; confirm settlement mapping separately.
validations: Compare original/follow-up approval reference in applicable reversal context.
Do not declare every subsequent message requires identical approval.
scenarios.expected: Scoped reference-match assertion; settlement remains unassessed.

scenarios.name: Approval Response Processing
scenarios.referenceClaim: Response code indicates approval; sale completed.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Interpret Element 83 by message/transaction context; distinguish full and partial approval before updating sale state.
validations: Use financial response mappings, not a universal success code.
Validate device state using response-bound execution.
scenarios.expected: Code interpretation does not by itself prove sale completion.

scenarios.name: Decline Response Processing
scenarios.referenceClaim: Response code indicates decline; sale rejected.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use financial-context decline mapping; do not classify communications-test approval code 1 without context.
validations: Keep decline distinct from timeout and malformed response.
Observe expected device behaviour with a defined simulator result.
scenarios.expected: Contextual decline handling, not a fabricated issuer decision.

scenarios.name: Partial Approval Indicator Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Indicator present and merchant enabled; partial approval enabled.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use Element 121 and applicable merchant/network support. Value 1 signals support; value 5 is an Amex-prepaid balance-only context, not generic Mastercard.
validations: Validate source-defined value and transaction applicability.
Keep configured network capability separate from field presence.
scenarios.expected: Indicator assertion only; no guaranteed issuer partial approval.

scenarios.name: Partial Approval Processing
scenarios.referenceClaim: Requested amount versus approved amount calculated; customer prompted for balance.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: In supported contexts interpret response F and approved amount Element 6; prompt for the remaining sale balance with independently established amount inputs.
validations: Bind original request, partial response and remaining balance.
Do not create synthetic approval evidence without labelling it.
scenarios.expected: Source-backed partial-response expectation; actual result Not Executed.

scenarios.name: Timeout Monitoring
scenarios.referenceClaim: 30-second timer initiated; await response.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Monitor the source-defined 30-second response interval and distinguish it from the separate TOR forwarding recommendation.
validations: Use deterministic clock/transport evidence.
Do not claim timer execution from a static request.
scenarios.expected: Timed observation only when transport test runs.

scenarios.name: Timeout Detection
scenarios.referenceClaim: No response before timer expiry; timeout triggered.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Include both absent and late responses; apply source-defined late-response handling.
validations: Test response before/after interval and no-response control.
Correlate timer to original device/request.
scenarios.expected: Timeout classification from transport evidence, not PAN/field checks.

scenarios.name: Timeout Reversal Generation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Original transaction timed out; TOR created.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Generate TOR only for a source-supported original context and apply queue, timing, retry and amount rules; authorization-only hold release uses cancellation, not an inferred TOR.
validations: Retain original identity and eligible transaction context.
Keep unresolved route/attempt/timing policy visible.
scenarios.expected: Flow-specific TOR checks; no universal timeout-to-TOR rule.

scenarios.name: Timeout Reversal Sequence Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: TOR uses original sequence; original matched.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Eligible TOR Element 86 must equal original Element 86; equality alone does not prove host matching.
validations: Bind explicit original and TOR IDs.
Test equal/mismatched sequence with valid controls.
scenarios.expected: Sequence-correlation predicate, not issuer/host acceptance.

scenarios.name: TOR Processing Order Validation
scenarios.referenceClaim: TOR sent before next financial message; queue priority enforced.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Section 2.3.1 supports queued TOR before the next request from that same device, or before settlement when no next request occurs; do not require a global queue across unrelated devices.
validations: Bind device, original, TOR and next request.
Apply transport-specific queue and offline recovery rules.
scenarios.expected: Scoped ordering expectation; not a global prohibition on concurrent requests.

scenarios.name: Receipt Generation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Authorization result available; customer receipt produced.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Generate source-required credit receipt content, use Mastercard receipt ID MC, mask account to last four digits and suppress expiry; include applicable outcome and partial-approval information.
validations: Inspect rendered receipt, not only request fields.
Separate normal, manual-entry and partial-approval expectations.
scenarios.expected: Receipt assertions only after output is supplied; Not Executed currently.

scenarios.name: Clearing Record Creation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Approval number captured; transaction available for clearing.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Use an authoritative clearing contract for record construction and eligibility; captured approval alone is insufficient.
validations: Bind original transaction, approval reference and clearing record.
Do not invent clearing fields from ATL105 purchase request.
scenarios.expected: Not assessed pending clearing contract and fixture.

scenarios.name: Settlement Preparation
scenarios.referenceClaim: Transaction data and amounts retained; settlement ready.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Establish settlement eligibility, record fields and amount reconciliation using the settlement contract.
validations: Keep settlement readiness separate from request/approval validity.
Require defined totals and original transaction references.
scenarios.expected: Not assessed pending settlement contract.

scenarios.name: Settlement Reporting
scenarios.referenceClaim: Settlement reporting supported; settled successfully.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Report successful settlement only from correlated settlement acknowledgement and reconciliation evidence.
validations: Retain actual result Not Executed until a run exists.
Distinguish submission, acceptance and reconciliation.
scenarios.expected: No success-shaped fallback when evidence is missing.

scenarios.name: Audit Logging
scenarios.referenceClaim: Request, response, timestamps and approvals retained; audit trail available.
scenarios.correctedRequirement: Define permitted audit events, correlation and retention through approved security policy; do not copy full request/response card data into logs by default.
validations: Use synthetic/redacted event examples.
Require policy for PAN masking, sensitive-data exclusion and access.
scenarios.expected: Audit/security checks unassessed until logging contract exists.
